Read the passage and answer the question.
Microfinance institutions extend small, collateral-free loans to borrowers who lack formal credit histories. Because many such borrowers are women in rural households, lenders often rely on group guarantees, where members of a group share responsibility for repayment. Critics argue that peer pressure within these groups can push borrowers into taking fresh loans merely to repay old ones.
According to the passage, why do lenders rely on group guarantees?
Because rural women prefer to borrow in large groups
Because peer pressure guarantees high profits for lenders
Because the borrowers usually cannot offer collateral or a credit record
Because the government requires every microloan to be guaranteed
The passage says the loans are collateral-free and the borrowers lack credit histories, so the group guarantee replaces these securities.

Read the passage and answer the question.
When a country's currency weakens, its exports become cheaper for foreign buyers, which can help exporters win orders. At the same time, imported goods such as crude oil and electronic components become costlier, and these higher costs can feed into domestic prices. Policymakers therefore rarely welcome a sharp fall in the currency, even if exporters gain from it.
Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
A weaker currency always lowers domestic inflation
A weaker currency has both benefits and costs for an economy
Exporters lose orders when the currency weakens
Policymakers prefer a sharp fall in the currency
The passage lists a gain (cheaper exports) and a cost (costlier imports feeding inflation), so the effect is mixed.

Read the passage and answer the question.
The new branch manager was known for her candid assessments; she told her team plainly where they had fallen short and what needed to change. Though some found her manner abrupt at first, most came to value her honesty.
Which word is most nearly the SAME in meaning as 'candid' as used in the passage?
'Candid' means open and honest; the passage confirms this with 'told her team plainly' and 'honesty'.

Choose the word that best fills the blank.
To curb rising inflation, the central bank decided to ________ the policy rate by 25 basis points.
Raising the policy rate makes borrowing costlier and reduces demand, which helps curb inflation.

Choose the word that best fills the blank.
Despite repeated reminders, the borrower failed to ________ the loan instalments on time.
A borrower 'repays' instalments; the other words do not collocate with 'loan instalments'.

Choose the pair of words that best fills both blanks.
The audit team was ________ to find that the records had been ________ maintained, with not a single entry missing.
'Not a single entry missing' shows careful record-keeping (meticulously), which would please the auditors.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Neither the manager nor his assistants (A) / was present in the branch (B) / when the auditors (C) / arrived on Monday morning. (D)
With 'neither…nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'assistants', so 'was' should be 'were'.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The committee submitted its report (A) / to the board last week (B) / after discussing about the proposal (C) / for several months. (D)
'Discuss' is a transitive verb and takes no preposition; it should be 'after discussing the proposal'.

Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part (in capitals). If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement required'.
Hardly had the customer left the branch THAN THE ALARM WENT OFF.
'Hardly' is followed by 'when' (or 'before'), not 'than', which pairs with 'no sooner'.

Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P: As a result, households began to move their savings from cash into bank accounts.
Q: Later, the government pushed banks to open branches in remote villages.
R: Some decades ago, many rural families had no safe place to keep their money.
S: Banks, in turn, could use these deposits to lend to local businesses.
R sets up the problem, Q gives the response, P its result ('As a result'), and S the follow-on effect ('in turn').
Choose the word most similar in meaning to PRUDENT.
Prudent means acting with care and good judgement, i.e. judicious.
Choose the word most opposite in meaning to FRUGAL.
Frugal means sparing with money; its opposite is extravagant.
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'To burn the midnight oil'.
To celebrate a festival with lamps
To work or study late into the night
The idiom refers to staying up late to work or study.
The correct spelling has a double 'c' and a double 'm': accommodation.

Choose the option that best replaces the part in capitals. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement required'.
IF I WOULD HAVE KNOWN about the holiday, I would have planned the trip earlier.
A past unreal condition uses the past perfect ('If I had known' or inverted 'Had I known'), not 'would have' in the if-clause.

What approximate value should come in place of the question mark (?)
24.98% of 639.97 + 17.02 × 11.99 = ?

What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the series?
7, 15, 32, 67, 138, ?

Two equations I and II are given. Solve both and choose the correct relationship between x and y.
I. x² − 11x + 30 = 0
II. y² − 15y + 56 = 0
x = 5, 6 (factors of 30 adding to 11); y = 7, 8. Every x is smaller than every y, so x < y.
The population of a town increased by 10% in the first year and decreased by 10% in the second year. If the population at the end of two years was 29,700, what was the initial population?
A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and allows a discount of 15%. If he earns a profit of ₹171, what is the cost price?
The difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and the simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 8% per annum is ₹96. What is the sum?
A and B started a business with ₹24,000 and ₹36,000 respectively. After 4 months, A invested ₹6,000 more and B withdrew ₹6,000. If the profit at the end of the year was ₹22,800, what is A's share?
A can complete a work in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work together for 4 days, after which A leaves. In how many more days will B finish the remaining work?
Together they do 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 per day; in 4 days 20/36 = 5/9. Remaining 4/9 × 18 = 8 days.

Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 minutes and 30 minutes respectively, while pipe C can empty the full tank in 15 minutes. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, in how much time will it be filled?
A train 240 m long crosses a platform 360 m long in 30 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
A boat covers 48 km downstream in 3 hours and the same distance upstream in 4 hours. How long will it take to cover 70 km in still water?
Downstream 16 km/h, upstream 12 km/h, so still-water speed = (16 + 12)/2 = 14 km/h; 70/14 = 5 hours.
A vessel contains 60 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 7 : 3. How many litres of water must be added to make the ratio 3 : 2?
The perimeter of a rectangle is 56 cm and its length is 4 cm more than its breadth. What is the area of a square whose side equals the diagonal of the rectangle?
l + b = 28, l − b = 4 → l = 16, b = 12; diagonal² = 256 + 144 = 400, which is the area of the square.
A bag contains 5 red, 4 blue and 3 green balls. Two balls are drawn at random. What is the probability that both are of the same colour?
Favourable = ⁵C₂ + ⁴C₂ + ³C₂ = 10 + 6 + 3 = 19; total = ¹²C₂ = 66; probability = 19/66.
In how many ways can the letters of the word BANKER be arranged so that the vowels always come together?
Treat A and E as one unit: 5 units → 5! = 120, and the vowels can swap in 2! ways: 120 × 2 = 240.

The table shows the number of loans (in hundreds) sanctioned by a bank branch.
Home loans: 2019 – 45, 2020 – 52
Car loans: 2019 – 30, 2020 – 36
Education loans: 2019 – 25, 2020 – 22
By what percentage did the total number of loans increase from 2019 to 2020?
The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 5 : 7. Eight years hence, the ratio will be 7 : 9. What is Q's present age?
The average of 11 results is 50. The average of the first six is 49 and that of the last six is 52. What is the sixth result?

Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G live on seven different floors of a building numbered 1 (lowest) to 7 (top).
• C lives on an even-numbered floor which is neither the lowest nor the highest even-numbered floor.
• Exactly two persons live between C and B.
• E lives above B.
• G lives immediately above E.
• Only one person lives between G and F.
• A lives on an even-numbered floor.
• D lives above F.
Who lives on the floor immediately above C?
C = 4; B = 1 (B = 7 fails as E is above B); E–G = 2–3 (other pairs clash), F = 5, A = 6, D = 7. Floor 5 is F.

Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G live on seven different floors of a building numbered 1 (lowest) to 7 (top).
• C lives on an even-numbered floor which is neither the lowest nor the highest even-numbered floor.
• Exactly two persons live between C and B.
• E lives above B.
• G lives immediately above E.
• Only one person lives between G and F.
• A lives on an even-numbered floor.
• D lives above F.
How many persons live between D and G?
Arrangement (1→7): B, E, G, C, F, A, D. Between D (7) and G (3) are C, F, A – three persons.

Six persons J, K, L, M, N and O sit in a row facing north.
• M sits at one of the extreme ends.
• Exactly two persons sit between M and J.
• K sits immediately to the left of M.
• L sits second to the left of O.
• N is not an immediate neighbour of J.
Who sits third from the right end?
K left of M forces M = 6, K = 5, J = 3; L and O take 2 and 4, N = 1. Order: N, L, J, O, K, M; third from right is O.

Statements: Only a few banks are branches. All branches are offices. No office is a vault.
Conclusions: I. Some banks are offices. II. No branch is a vault.
Some banks are branches and all branches are offices, so some banks are offices. Branches lie inside offices, which have nothing in common with vaults, so no branch is a vault.

Statements: Some coins are notes. All notes are cheques. No cheque is a draft.
Conclusions: I. Some coins are not drafts. II. Some notes are drafts.
The coins that are notes are cheques and hence not drafts, so I follows. Notes lie within cheques, which have no drafts, so II is false.

Statements: P ≥ Q > R = S; T < S ≤ U
Conclusions: I. P > T  II. U > R
P ≥ Q > R = S > T gives P > T. U ≥ S = R gives only U ≥ R, so II does not follow.
Introducing Arjun, Kavya says, 'His father is the only son of my father.' How is Arjun related to Kavya?
The only son of Kavya's father is Kavya's brother; Arjun is his son, so Arjun is Kavya's nephew.

A + B means A is the mother of B; A − B means A is the brother of B; A × B means A is the wife of B; A ÷ B means A is the father of B.
If P + Q − R ÷ S × T, how is T related to P?
P is mother of Q, Q is brother of R, so R is P's child; R (male, a father) is father of S; S (female, a wife) is P's granddaughter, and T is her husband.
Ravi walks 10 m north, turns right and walks 6 m, turns right again and walks 18 m, then turns left and walks 9 m. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?
Positions: (0,10) → (6,10) → (6,−8) → (15,−8). Distance = √(15² + 8²) = 17 m towards the south-east.
In a certain code language, BRANCH is written as CTDRHN. How is LOAN written in that code?
Letters are shifted +1, +2, +3, +4, … in order: L+1 = M, O+2 = Q, A+3 = D, N+4 = R.
In a code language, 'save money now' is written as 'la pi ko', 'money is safe' as 'tu pi re', and 'now is time' as 're ko zu'. What is the code for 'safe'?
money = pi (1st & 2nd), now = ko (1st & 3rd), is = re (2nd & 3rd); so in 'money is safe', safe = tu.
In a row of 40 students, Meena is 14th from the left end and Sahil is 19th from the right end. How many students sit between them?
Sahil is 40 − 19 + 1 = 22nd from the left; between 14th and 22nd are 22 − 14 − 1 = 7 students.

Study the arrangement:
7 K # 3 B @ M 9 % E 2 R & 5 T U 8 $ W 4
How many symbols are immediately preceded by a number and immediately followed by a letter?
Only '9 % E' and '8 $ W' satisfy the condition.

A word-arrangement machine works as follows: in each step, the word that comes first in alphabetical order among the words not yet arranged is placed to the immediate right of the words already arranged at the left end; other words keep their order.
Input: tank vote echo pin rise blue
Which of the following is Step 3?
blue echo pin tank vote rise
blue echo tank vote pin rise
blue echo pin rise tank vote
blue echo pin vote tank rise
Step 1: blue tank vote echo pin rise; Step 2: blue echo tank vote pin rise; Step 3: blue echo pin tank vote rise.
Among P, Q, R, S and T, each of a different height: Q is taller than only R and T. S is shorter than P. T is taller than R. Who is the tallest?
Q is taller than exactly two (R, T), so Q is third tallest and P, S are above Q; S < P makes P the tallest.

Statements: M ≥ N = O < P ≤ Q
Conclusions: I. Q > O  II. M > O
Q ≥ P > O gives Q > O. M ≥ N = O gives M ≥ O only, so II does not follow.
Facing east, Neha walks 12 m, turns left and walks 5 m. She then turns left again and walks 24 m. Which direction is she now from her starting point?
Positions: (12,0) → (12,5) → (−12,5). She is 12 m west and 5 m north of the start, i.e. north-west.
ibps-clerk:
Read the passage and answer the question.
Ramesh, a small shopkeeper, opened a recurring deposit account and saved a fixed amount every month. When his daughter got admission to college three years later, he was able to pay her fees without borrowing from a moneylender.
What helped Ramesh pay his daughter's fees?
Regular monthly savings in a recurring deposit
The passage says he saved a fixed amount every month in a recurring deposit and so did not need to borrow.

Read the passage and answer the question.
Many people ignore the small print on loan documents. Hidden charges such as processing fees and prepayment penalties can raise the real cost of a loan considerably. Reading every clause before signing can save a borrower a lot of money.
What is the main advice given in the passage?
Avoid taking any loans at all
Always choose the bank with the most branches
Pay prepayment penalties as early as possible
Read all the terms of a loan carefully before signing
The last sentence states the advice directly: read every clause before signing.

Read the passage and answer the question.
The flood had damaged the village bridge, so the bank's mobile van could not reach the market. The officials decided to set up a temporary counter in the school building instead.
What does the word 'temporary' mean as used in the passage?
Lasting for only a short time
The counter was a stop-gap arrangement until the van could return, i.e. lasting only a short time.

Choose the word that best fills the blank.
She was so tired after the long journey that she fell ________ as soon as she lay down.

Choose the word that best fills the blank.
The bank will remain ________ on Sunday.
After 'remain', an adjective is needed; 'closed' describes the state of the bank.

Choose the word that best fills the blank.
He has been working in this branch ________ 2019.
'Since' is used with a point of time (2019) in the perfect continuous tense.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Each of the students (A) / have submitted (B) / the assignment (C) / on time. (D)
'Each of' takes a singular verb: 'has submitted'.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
She is one of the best (A) / cashier who have (B) / ever worked (C) / at this branch. (D)
'One of the best' must be followed by a plural noun: 'cashiers who have'.

Choose the option that best replaces the part in capitals. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement required'.
He DID NOT KNEW the answer.
After the auxiliary 'did', the base form of the verb is used: 'did not know'.

Rearrange the sentences to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: Finally, she deposited the cheque at the bank counter.
Q: First, Anita checked the date and amount on the cheque.
R: After filling in the slip, she signed on the back of the cheque.
S: Next, she filled in the deposit slip.
First (Q) → Next, the slip (S) → After filling the slip (R) → Finally (P).
Choose the word most similar in meaning to ABUNDANT.
Abundant means existing in large quantities, i.e. plentiful.
Choose the word most opposite in meaning to ANCIENT.
Ancient means very old; its opposite is modern.
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'A piece of cake'.
'A piece of cake' describes a task that is very easy.
Which of the following words is spelt correctly?
The correct spelling has one 'c' and a double 's': necessary.
Choose the one word for: 'A person who lends money at very high rates of interest'.
A usurer lends money at excessive interest; a debtor is a borrower.

What will come in place of the question mark (?)
35% of 480 + 18² − 125 = ?

What approximate value should come in place of the question mark (?)
19.97 × 15.02 − 149.99 ÷ 5.01 = ?

What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the series?
3, 8, 18, 38, 78, ?

Two equations I and II are given. Solve both and choose the correct relationship between x and y.
I. x² = 49
II. y² − 14y + 49 = 0
x = +7 or −7; (y − 7)² = 0 gives y = 7. So x is either equal to or less than y: x ≤ y.
40% of a number is 64 more than 20% of the same number. What is the number?
40% − 20% = 20% of the number = 64, so the number = 64 × 5 = 320.
By selling an article for ₹1,035, a shopkeeper gains 15%. What is its cost price?
What is the difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and the simple interest on ₹5,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum?
A invested ₹15,000 for 12 months and B invested ₹20,000 for 6 months in a business. Out of a total profit of ₹10,000, what is A's share?
The average of five numbers is 28. If one number is removed, the average of the remaining four becomes 25. What is the removed number?
Total of five = 140, total of four = 100, so the removed number = 40.
A father is three times as old as his son. After 12 years, he will be twice as old as his son. What is the son's present age?
A can do a piece of work in 10 days and B in 15 days. In how many days can they finish it working together?
Pipe A can fill a tank in 6 hours and pipe B in 12 hours. If both are opened together, in how many hours will the empty tank be filled?
A train 150 m long passes an electric pole in 9 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
A 40-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How much water should be added so that the ratio becomes 5 : 3?
The circumference of a circle is 88 cm. What is its area? (Take π = 22/7)
Two fair dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is 8?

The table shows mobile phones sold by four shops in a month.
Shop P – 240, Shop Q – 180, Shop R – 300, Shop S – 280
What percentage of the total sales was made by shop R?

Five friends P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing north. R sits in the middle. Q sits at the extreme right end. T sits immediately to the left of R. P is not an immediate neighbour of Q.
Who sits between R and Q?
R = 3, Q = 5, T = 2; P cannot be at 4 (next to Q), so P = 1 and S = 4, which is between R and Q.

Five boxes A, B, C, D and E are kept one above the other. C is at the top. Only one box is kept between C and A. B is kept immediately below A. D is not at the bottom.
Which box is at the bottom?
From top: C (5), A (3), B (2); D cannot be at 1, so D = 4 and E is at the bottom.

Five persons F, G, H, I and J attend a training programme on different days from Monday to Friday. H attends on Wednesday. Exactly two persons attend between G and F. I attends on a day after F. J attends immediately before H. F does not attend on Monday.
Who attends on Friday?
J = Tuesday. G and F must be Monday/Thursday; F is not Monday, so G = Mon, F = Thu, and I (after F) = Friday.

Statements: All pens are books. Some books are bags.
Conclusions: I. Some pens are bags. II. Some bags are books.
Pens and bags need not overlap, so I does not follow. 'Some books are bags' converts to 'some bags are books', so II follows.

Statements: No apple is a mango. All mangoes are fruits.
Conclusions: I. Some fruits are not apples. II. No fruit is an apple.
The fruits that are mangoes are not apples, so I follows. Other fruits may be apples, so II is not definite.

Statements: M ≥ N = O < P ≤ Q
Conclusions: I. M ≥ O  II. Q > N
M ≥ N = O gives M ≥ O. Q ≥ P > O = N gives Q > N. Both follow.
A is the sister of B. C is the mother of B. D is the father of C. How is A related to D?
A is C's daughter (sister of C's child B), and D is C's father, so A is D's granddaughter.
Pointing to a boy, Rina said, 'He is the son of the only son of my father's father.' How is the boy related to Rina?
The only son of Rina's father's father is Rina's father; his son is Rina's brother.
Sita walks 5 km east, turns left and walks 3 km, then turns left again and walks 5 km. Where is she now with respect to her starting point?
Positions: (5,0) → (5,3) → (0,3), i.e. 3 km due north of the start.
Amit is facing north. He turns 90° clockwise, then 180° anticlockwise, and then 45° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
North → 90° clockwise = East → 180° anticlockwise = West → 45° clockwise = North-West.
If CAT is coded as 24 (sum of letter positions), what is the code for DOG?
If MONEY is coded as NPOFZ, how is CASH coded?
Each letter is moved one step forward: C→D, A→B, S→T, H→I.
Rohit is 9th from the top and 26th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in the class?
In a row, Ajay is 12th from the left and Vijay is 8th from the right. When they interchange their positions, Ajay becomes 20th from the left. How many persons are in the row?
Ajay's new position is Vijay's old one: 20th from left and 8th from right, so total = 20 + 8 − 1 = 27.

Study the arrangement:
4 A 7 # K 2 P @ 9 B $ 3 M & 6
How many letters are immediately followed by a number?
If the English alphabet is written in reverse order, which letter will be 7th to the right of the 10th letter from the left?
In reverse order, the 10th + 7 = 17th letter from the left is the 27 − 17 = 10th letter of the normal alphabet, J.
All others are perfect cubes (3³, 4³, 5³, 6³); 144 is 12², not a cube.

sbi-po:
Read the passage and answer the question.
Behavioural economists have found that people often prefer a smaller reward today over a larger one in the future, even when waiting would clearly make them better off. This tendency, known as present bias, helps explain why many people under-save for retirement. Automatic enrolment in pension schemes, where employees must actively opt out rather than opt in, has been shown to raise participation sharply.
Which feature of automatic enrolment, as described in the passage, raises participation?
It offers employees a larger reward today
Employees must take action to stay out rather than to join
It removes present bias from people's minds
Employees are legally barred from opting out
The passage says employees 'must actively opt out rather than opt in', so inertia keeps them enrolled.

Read the passage and answer the question.
A bank's capital acts as a cushion against unexpected losses. If a bank holds too little capital, even a modest rise in bad loans can wipe out its equity and threaten depositors. Regulators therefore require banks to hold capital in proportion to the riskiness of their assets, so that riskier lending must be backed by more capital.
Which of the following statements is supported by the passage?
Banks with more capital never face bad loans
Regulators prohibit banks from making risky loans
Depositors are protected only by the government
A bank that makes riskier loans must hold more capital against them
The last sentence states that riskier lending must be backed by more capital.

Read the passage and answer the question.
The report praises the scheme for widening access to credit but warns that rapid expansion without proper checks could lead to a rise in defaults. It recommends stronger verification of borrowers before further growth.
The report's attitude towards the scheme is best described as:
It praises the scheme but adds warnings and safeguards, which is cautious support.

Choose the word that best fills the blank.
The new policy is expected to ________ the flow of credit to small businesses, which had slowed down sharply.
Since credit had slowed, the policy is expected to increase (boost) it; the other words mean reduce or stop.

Choose the word that best fills the blank.
The speaker's arguments were so ________ that even the sceptics in the audience were convinced.

Choose the pair of words that best fills both blanks.
The bank's bad loans ________ sharply after it ________ its credit appraisal process, rejecting weak applications early.
Rejecting weak applications means the process was tightened, which would reduce (decline) bad loans.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Not only the borrowers (A) / but also the guarantor (B) / were informed (C) / about the default notice. (D)
With 'not only…but also', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'guarantor': 'was informed'.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
The new rules, which came into effect (A) / last month, has made (B) / it easier for customers (C) / to open accounts online. (D)
The subject 'rules' is plural, so it should be 'have made'.

Choose the option that best replaces the part in capitals. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement required'.
The manager insisted that every clerk COMPLETES the training by Friday.
After 'insist that', the subjunctive base form is used: 'every clerk complete'.

Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P: However, these gains can vanish quickly if borrowers lose their incomes.
Q: Easy credit allows households to buy homes and vehicles they could not otherwise afford.
R: That is why lenders are told to assess not just a borrower's present income but its stability.
S: When repayments stop, both the household and the lender suffer.
Q introduces the benefit, P adds the caveat ('However'), S states the consequence, and R gives the lesson ('That is why').
Choose the word most similar in meaning to MITIGATE.
Mitigate means to make less severe, i.e. alleviate; aggravate is its opposite.
Choose the word most opposite in meaning to OBSCURE.
Obscure means unclear or hidden; evident means clear and obvious.
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'To bite the bullet'.
To face a painful situation bravely
The idiom means to accept and endure something unpleasant with courage.

Choose the word that can fill both blanks appropriately.
(i) He deposited the money in his savings ________.
(ii) Please give a brief ________ of what happened.
'Savings account' and 'an account of what happened' both use 'account'.
She is living in Pune since 2015.
She has been lived in Pune since 2015.
She has lived in Pune since 2015.
An action continuing from a past point ('since 2015') takes the present perfect: 'has lived'.

What approximate value should come in place of the question mark (?)
√624.8 × 7.96 + 39.97% of 449.9 = ?

Find the wrong number in the series:
4, 9, 25, 49, 121, 169, 288
The series is squares of consecutive primes: 2², 3², 5², 7², 11², 13², 17² = 289, not 288.

What will come in place of the question mark (?)
12, 14, 19, 29, 46, ?

Two equations I and II are given. Solve both and choose the correct relationship between x and y.
I. x² − 4x − 21 = 0
II. y² + 9y + 18 = 0
x = 7 or −3; y = −3 or −6. Every x is greater than or equal to every y (−3 = −3), so x ≥ y.

In an election between two candidates, 10% of the voters did not vote and 1,000 votes cast were invalid. The winner got 54% of the valid votes and won by 1,000 votes. How many voters were on the list?
Margin = 54% − 46% = 8% of valid votes = 1,000 → valid = 12,500; votes cast = 13,500 = 90% of voters → 15,000.
A trader sells two articles for ₹1,980 each. On one he gains 10% and on the other he loses 10%. What is his overall result?
A sum of money amounts to ₹13,310 in 3 years at 10% per annum compounded annually. What is the sum?
A, B and C start a business with investments in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. After 6 months, A doubles his investment. If the annual profit is ₹40,500, what is B's share?
Five years ago, the average age of A and B was 25 years. At present, the average age of A, B and C is 30 years. What will be C's age after 5 years?
A + B now = 2×25 + 10 = 60; A + B + C = 90 → C = 30, so after 5 years C = 35.
A is 50% more efficient than B. Working together, they finish a work in 18 days. In how many days can A alone finish it?
Efficiency A : B = 3 : 2; total work = (3 + 2) × 18 = 90 units; A alone = 90/3 = 30 days.
A pipe can fill a tank in 8 hours. Because of a leak at the bottom, it takes 10 hours to fill. In how many hours can the leak empty the full tank?
Two trains of lengths 180 m and 220 m run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 54 km/h and 90 km/h. How long will they take to cross each other completely?
Relative speed = 144 km/h = 40 m/s; distance = 400 m; time = 10 s.
The speed of a boat in still water is 15 km/h. It goes 36 km downstream and returns to the starting point in a total of 5 hours. What is the speed of the stream?
A container holds 80 litres of pure milk. 8 litres are taken out and replaced with water. This process is carried out three times in all. How much milk is left in the container?
A right circular cone has base radius 6 cm and height 8 cm. What is its total surface area?
Slant height = √(36 + 64) = 10; TSA = πr(l + r) = π × 6 × 16 = 96π cm².
Two cards are drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. What is the probability that both are kings or both are queens?
A committee of 5 is to be formed from 6 men and 4 women. In how many ways can it be formed if it must contain at least 3 men?

Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F sit around a circular table facing the centre.
• B sits third to the left of A.
• E sits immediately to the right of B.
• C is an immediate neighbour of E.
• D is not an immediate neighbour of B.
Who sits immediately to the left of F?
Clockwise from A: A, C, E, B, F, D (right = anticlockwise when facing the centre). F's immediate left is D.

Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F sit around a circular table facing the centre.
• B sits third to the left of A.
• E sits immediately to the right of B.
• C is an immediate neighbour of E.
• D is not an immediate neighbour of B.
Who sits second to the right of D?
Clockwise order A, C, E, B, F, D. Moving right (anticlockwise) from D: F, then B.

Seven persons P, Q, R, S, T, U and V were born in January, March, April, June, August, September and November of the same year, one in each month.
• P was born in a month having 30 days.
• Exactly three persons were born between P and S.
• T was born immediately before P.
• Q was born in a month having 31 days, but not in January.
• U was born immediately after Q.
• V was born after P but before Q.
Who was born in June?
Q in March leaves no room for V between P and Q, so Q = Aug, U = Sep; V between P and Q forces P = Apr, V = Jun, T = Mar, S = Nov, R = Jan.

Seven persons P, Q, R, S, T, U and V were born in January, March, April, June, August, September and November of the same year, one in each month.
• P was born in a month having 30 days.
• Exactly three persons were born between P and S.
• T was born immediately before P.
• Q was born in a month having 31 days, but not in January.
• U was born immediately after Q.
• V was born after P but before Q.
How many persons were born between T and U?
Order: R (Jan), T (Mar), P (Apr), V (Jun), Q (Aug), U (Sep), S (Nov). Between T and U are P, V and Q.

Statements: Only a few loans are secured. All secured items are insured.
Conclusions: I. Some loans are not secured. II. All secured items are definitely loans.

Statements: No branch is a vault. Some vaults are lockers. All lockers are safes.
Conclusions: I. Some safes are not branches. II. Some lockers are not branches.
The lockers that are vaults cannot be branches (II), and those lockers are safes, so some safes are not branches (I).

'P @ Q' means P ≥ Q; 'P # Q' means P > Q; 'P $ Q' means P = Q; 'P % Q' means P < Q.
Statements: A # B, B @ C, C $ D, D % E
Conclusions: I. A # D  II. E # B
A > B ≥ C = D < E. So A > D (I follows); E and B cannot be compared (II does not follow).

Statements: J > K ≥ L; L < M ≤ N; O ≥ K
Conclusions: I. O > L  II. O = L
O ≥ K ≥ L gives O ≥ L; neither part is certain alone, but one of them must be true, so either I or II follows.

In a family of six — P, Q, R, S, T and U — P is married to T. Q is the son of T. U is the wife of Q. R and S are U's children. S is a girl and R is S's brother.
How is S related to P?
Q is the son of P and T; S is the daughter of Q and U, so S is P's granddaughter.
Point A is 12 m west of point B. Point C is 5 m north of B. Point D is 7 m south of A, and point E is 7 m east of D. What is the distance between E and C, and in which direction is C from E?
In a code language, 'market rates rise' is written as 'mo ta ki', 'rates fall today' as 'su ta ne', and 'today market opens' as 'ne pa mo'. What is the code for 'rise'?
market = mo, rates = ta, today = ne (common words); so in the first sentence, rise = ki.
In a certain code, CREDIT is written as FSDUJE. Following the same rule, how is SAVING written?
Split into halves, reverse each (CRE→ERC, DIT→TID) and shift each letter +1. SAV→VAS→WBT, ING→GNI→HOJ.
In a class of 45 students, Neha's rank from the top is 4 more than twice her rank from the bottom. What is her rank from the top?
Let bottom rank = b: (2b + 4) + b − 1 = 45 → b = 14, so top rank = 32.

B is 3rd lightest. D < A < E with E not heaviest forces E = 4th, A = 2nd, D = lightest; so C is the heaviest.
Just before sunset, Arun stands with his shadow falling directly behind him. Which direction is he facing?
Near sunset the sun is in the west and shadows fall to the east; with the shadow behind him, he faces west.

Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a row facing north.
• G sits exactly in the middle of the row.
• A and D are the immediate neighbours of G.
• E sits at one of the extreme ends.
• Only one person sits between E and D.
• C sits second to the left of A.
• B sits second to the left of G.
Who sits immediately to the right of B?
If A were 5th, C would be 3rd = D's seat; so A = 3, D = 5, E = 7, C = 1, B = 2, F = 6. Right of B is A.

Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a row facing north.

• E sits at one of the extreme ends.
• Only one person sits between E and D.
• C sits second to the left of A.
• B sits second to the left of G.
How many persons sit between C and F?
Order: C, B, A, G, D, F, E. Between C (1) and F (6): B, A, G, D.

Five persons V, W, X, Y and Z live on the five floors of a building numbered 1 (lowest) to 5 (top). Z lives on an odd-numbered floor but not on the top floor. Y lives immediately below Z. W lives below Y. X lives above V.
Who lives on the floor immediately above Z?
Z = 3 (Z = 1 leaves no room below for Y), Y = 2, W = 1; X above V gives V = 4, X = 5.

Statements: Some cards are coins. Some coins are notes.
Conclusions: I. Some cards are notes. II. No card is a note.

X is the son of Y. Y is the sister of Z. Z is the father of W. How is X related to W?

From her house, Pooja walks 8 m south, then turns right and walks 6 m. What is the shortest distance between her and her house?

In the morning, the shadow of a tower falls exactly towards Ravi's right. Which direction is Ravi facing?

If BANK is coded as YZMP, how is LOAN coded?

How many pairs of letters are there in the word BRANCH which have as many letters between them in the word as in the English alphabet (in either direction)?

rbi-b: Under which Act was the Reserve Bank of India constituted?
The RBI was set up under the RBI Act, 1934 and began operations in April 1935.
Under the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), a scheduled bank must keep a specified share of its net demand and time liabilities in which form?
As a cash balance with the RBI
As gold in its own vaults
As government securities in its own portfolio
As deposits with other commercial banks
CRR is maintained as cash balances with the RBI; liquid assets held by the bank itself count towards SLR, not CRR.
Which RBI facility allows scheduled banks to borrow overnight, at a rate above the policy repo rate, by dipping into their SLR holdings up to a limit?
The MSF is a penal-rate overnight window above the repo rate under which banks may use a portion of their SLR securities.
When the RBI purchases government securities in the open market, what is the immediate effect on liquidity in the banking system?
Liquidity is injected into the system
Liquidity is absorbed from the system
The RBI pays for the securities it buys, adding reserves (rupee liquidity) to the banking system.
Which body determines the policy repo rate in India under the flexible inflation targeting framework?
Securities and Exchange Board of India
Under the amended RBI Act, the Monetary Policy Committee decides the policy repo rate.
How many members make up the Monetary Policy Committee constituted under the RBI Act, 1934?
The MPC has six members: three from the RBI (including the Governor) and three external members appointed by the Government.
Which price index is used to define the inflation target under India's flexible inflation targeting framework?
The target is set in terms of headline CPI (Combined) inflation.
As per RBI's prudential norms, a term loan generally becomes a Non-Performing Asset when interest or principal instalment remains overdue for more than how many days?
Under the income recognition and asset classification norms, an asset is an NPA if dues remain overdue for more than 90 days.
Which Act enables secured creditors such as banks to enforce their security interest without the intervention of a court?
The SARFAESI Act lets secured lenders take possession of and sell secured assets without going to court.
Which of the following activities is a payments bank NOT permitted to undertake?
Payments banks may accept deposits, issue debit cards and offer remittances, but they cannot lend or issue credit cards.
Which RBI function refers to providing emergency liquidity support to a solvent bank facing a temporary cash shortage?
As lender of last resort, the RBI supplies emergency funds to banks to prevent a liquidity crisis spreading.
Which authority issues the one-rupee note in India?
One-rupee notes and coins are issued by the Government of India (Ministry of Finance); higher-denomination notes are issued by the RBI.
Fiscal deficit of the Government is best defined as:
Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings
Value of imports minus value of exports
Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts); the other options define revenue deficit, primary deficit and trade deficit.
Gross National Product (GNP) is equal to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) plus:
GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad; depreciation and indirect taxes link gross/net and market-price/factor-cost measures.
Stagflation refers to an economic situation marked by:
High inflation along with stagnant growth and high unemployment
Falling prices along with rapid growth
Low inflation along with full employment
A sustained fall in the general price level
Stagflation combines rising prices with economic stagnation and unemployment.
Which monetary aggregate is commonly referred to as 'broad money' in India?
M1 is narrow money and M0 is reserve money; M3 (M1 + time deposits with banks) is broad money.
Where is the headquarters of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS)?
The BIS, often called the central bank of central banks, is headquartered in Basel.
Which institution was established along with the International Monetary Fund at the Bretton Woods Conference of 1944?
International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
The 1944 Bretton Woods Conference created the IMF and the IBRD; the WTO was set up only in 1995.
Which national financial inclusion mission, launched in 2014, aims to provide every household with a basic bank account along with a RuPay debit card?
PMJDY, launched in August 2014, focuses on universal access to basic banking accounts with RuPay cards.
Which of the following is a qualitative (selective) tool of credit control rather than a quantitative one?
Moral suasion (persuasion of banks) is qualitative; CRR, OMOs and the bank rate act on the overall quantity of credit.

It removes the trade-off between inflation and unemployment
It allows the bank to keep interest rates unchanged permanently

The sceptics' argument is best described as:
A claim that targeted schemes have no exclusion errors
A dilemma between adequacy and affordability
An objection based on administrative complexity
A demand that transfers be linked to employment

Eight persons A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H live on eight different floors of a building numbered 1 (lowest) to 8 (top).
• D lives on an odd-numbered floor above floor 3.
• Exactly two persons live between D and C.
• A lives on an even-numbered floor below D.
• G lives immediately above C.
• E lives below C.
• Exactly four persons live between E and H.
• B lives immediately above H.
Who lives on floor 3?

D = 5 or 7. If D = 7, then C = 4, G = 5 and E (floor 1–3) puts H on 6, 7 or 8, but B must be immediately above H on a free floor — impossible. So D = 5, C = 2, G = 3, E = 1, H = 6, B = 7, A = 4, F = 8.
